name: Kaspi.kz

logo.source: commons.wikimedia.org (File:Kaspi.kz logo.svg; Wikipedia infobox logo field empty)

description: Kaspi.kz is Kazakhstan's dominant consumer super-app: about 68% of its monthly users open it daily (10.7 million daily users at 2025-12-31). One app handles paying in shops and online (Payments), buying goods, travel and tickets from merchants (Marketplace) and borrowing, buy-now-pay-later and saving (Fintech). The three feed each other: payments and shopping bring users in, and the bank turns them into borrowers funded mostly by local-currency deposits. Fintech interest income is the biggest single profit pool. In 2025-26 it is spreading into Turkey: it owns Hepsiburada (a Turkish e-commerce marketplace) and completed the purchase of Rabobank A.S. in July 2026, rebranded Hepsi Bank. Net income is flat (KZT259B in Q2 2026) because of higher deposit funding costs and Turkish investments.

businessLines.name: Marketplace
businessLines.shareBasis: 1,028,033 / 2,239,675, the sum of the three segments before intergroup eliminations of 24,824 (computed)
businessLines.how: Fees taken from merchants on each sale (3P take rate 16.1% in Q2 2026, up 160 bps, helped by advertising and delivery fees); plus retail revenue where Kaspi sells goods itself (Turkey, e-grocery); plus a small amount of interest and other gains.
businessLines.description: e-Commerce (online shopping, mostly third-party merchants, and in Turkey a hybrid 1P/3P model), m-Commerce (in-store shopping in the app), Kaspi Travel, e-Grocery, e-Cars, and Hepsiburada in Turkey.

businessLines.name: Fintech
businessLines.how: Interest earned on the loan book (net interest income after paying depositors), plus fees; revenue is mainly interest income, with the cost of funding (14.5% average in Q2 2026, up 150 bps) and cost of risk (0.7% in Q2 2026) as the swing factors.
businessLines.description: Consumer and merchant loans, buy-now-pay-later, deposits, all inside the app; lends only in tenge, funded mainly by local-currency savings accounts.

revenue.note: vs 713,528 in H1 2025 (+24%); Q2 2026 KZT454,915M (+23%, about $946M); interest revenue 839,115 and fee revenue 50,944 in H1 2026 (fee revenue fell from 105,950)

businessLines.name: Payments
businessLines.how: Fees on the value of payments processed (total payment volume, TPV) plus some interest revenue; also the main way Kaspi acquires and engages customers.
businessLines.description: Consumer payments (QR, cards, bills, peer-to-peer) and merchant acceptance, invoicing and supplier payments; includes Kaspi Alaqan pay-by-palm.

brands.name: Hepsiburada
brands.note: Turkish e-commerce platform founded 2000; ownership percentage not extracted; the weaker lira (down 21% vs tenge YoY) depresses reported growth

brands.name: Hepsi Bank (formerly Rabobank A.S.)
brands.note: Acquisition completed July 2026; a shopping loan integrated into Hepsiburada is being piloted, wider rollout from 2027

brands.name: Kasper
brands.note: AI shopping assistant rolled out from July 2026; about 20% of eligible consumers used it within a month (company)

whatsNext.text: Proposed dividend increase to KZT1,000 per ADS, pending shareholder approval; Hepsi Bank shopping-loan pilot with wider Turkish fintech rollout from 2027
